run.request: We want to redo our small galley kitchen for $25,000 or less. We are keeping the layout, but want new cabinets, counters, a backsplash and appliances. Where should the money go, what order do we do things in, and what usually goes wrong?
run.title: Galley kitchen redo for $25,000 or less
run.goal: Split your budget, order the work, and avoid the usual galley mistakes.
run.summary: Put about $9,000 into cabinets and $4,500 into appliances, and hold a $3,500 reserve. Pick appliances first, template counters after cabinets, and watch the aisle width.

body.text: These are estimated ranges. If every line hits its high end, you go over $25,000, so aim low to mid and protect the reserve.
The labor line covers cabinet install, demo help, hookups and permits. Counter install is already in the counter price.

items: Spend on cabinet boxes and drawer hardware, since you use them daily.
Spend on a quiet dishwasher and a good range hood.
Spend on licensed pros for any wiring or pipe changes.
Keep the 10 to 15 percent reserve for surprises found at demo.
Save with stock or semi-custom cabinets in standard sizes.
Save with simple subway or ceramic tile for the backsplash.
Save by buying appliances as a package or on holiday sales.
Save by doing your own demo and haul-away.

sections.heading: Picking cabinets and counters

body.text: In a 20 to 25 ft galley, stock or RTA cabinets leave the most money for counters and appliances. Semi-custom fits only at the low to middle of its range.
Semi-custom for 20 to 25 ft runs an estimated $6,000 to $15,000, past the $11,000 cabinet line. Stay near $300 to $440 per ft, or use semi-custom on one wall and stock on the other.

items: Range: 30 in (76 cm) standard, or 24 in (61 cm) to save space.
Fridge: counter-depth, about 24 in (61 cm) deep, flush with cabinets.
Dishwasher: 24 in (61 cm) standard, or 18 in (46 cm) for tight runs.
Microwave: over-the-range or drawer style keeps counters clear.
Open doors must still leave at least 42 in (107 cm) of aisle.
Keep the dishwasher from facing the fridge door.

body.text: Prices are 2026 estimates. Cabinets are priced per linear ft for product and delivery, and counters per sq ft installed.

revised: Aisle check says 36 to 42 in. Change to at least 42 in (107 cm) to match the checks.
Semi-custom at $300-$600/ft for 20-25 ft is $6,000-$15,000. Say the high end exceeds the $11,000 cabinet line.
Prices say install included, but budget-split has a separate labor line. Clarify which costs are in labor.

sections.heading: Order of the work

body.text: Order cabinets and appliances before you demo. The estimated 4 to 8 weeks of work starts at demo, so wait for firm delivery dates.

items: Pick appliances and get spec sheets before ordering cabinets.
Measure, then order cabinets. Lead times run an estimated 1 to 10 weeks.
Demo only after cabinet and appliance delivery dates are confirmed.
Fix wiring and plumbing while walls are open, then pass inspection.
Drywall and paint before any cabinets go in.
Set the cabinets, then have the counter shop template them.
Do the backsplash after counters, then appliances and final touches.

rows: Final sizes, appliance spec sheets, place orders

revised: Step 1 lead times of 2 to 8 weeks conflict with semi-custom at 4 to 10 weeks. Use 1 to 10 weeks.
Add one line: pick appliances and get spec sheets before ordering cabinets.

body.text: Most galley problems come from tight space and bad timing. Measure every door swing, order early, and keep your reserve for what demo uncovers.

items: Call a licensed electrician for any new circuit, moved outlet or under-cabinet light wiring.
Counter outlets must be GFCI protected. Have the electrician confirm this at rough-in.
Call a licensed plumber for leaks, new shutoff valves or dishwasher drain changes.
Gas range hookup goes to a licensed plumber or gas fitter, never DIY.
Stop demo and call a pro for soft subfloor, mold or old wiring.

rows: Draw every door swing to scale
Check level, plan shims and scribe
Get spec sheets before cabinet order
Check amps and plug type early

next_steps: Measure the kitchen and draw every door swing to scale.
Pick appliances and get their spec sheets.
Get cabinet, counter and labor quotes against the sample plan.
Order cabinets and appliances, then confirm delivery dates.
Schedule demo, electrician and plumber once dates are firm.
assumptions: US prices, mid-range finishes, 2026 cost estimates.
About 20 to 25 linear ft of cabinets.
Plumbing, gas and electric stay in place.
Licensed contractor does most work, you handle some demo.
Cabinet install is in labor, counter install in counter price.
checks: Budget ranges add up to $25,000 or less, with reserve
Counter templating comes after cabinets are installed
Appliances are picked before cabinets are ordered
Aisle clearance of at least 42 in (1,067 mm) is mentioned
All prices are labeled as estimates with a range
conflicts: Aisle width: choices says 36 to 42 in (91 to 107 cm), pitfalls says aim for 42 in (107 cm).
Cabinet lead time: choices gives semi-custom 4 to 10 weeks, work-order says lead times are often 2 to 8 weeks.
Install costs: choices prices cabinets and counters as installed, budget-split adds a separate $3,000 to $5,000 labor line.
Cabinet cost: choices semi-custom range for 20 to 25 ft ($6,000 to $15,000) goes past budget-split's $8,000 to $11,000 cabinet line.
